clue.text: A writer having fine point

parts.note: feeling fine means feeling well
S is a point of the compass, south

explanation.surface: A novelist equipped with a fine-nibbed pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine point' reads as a pen nib, but it splits into two pieces. H. G. Wells wrote The Time Machine.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells was the English author of The War of the Worlds, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Servant wearing a very short skirt

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
something you are wearing is on you

explanation.surface: A housemaid dressed in a miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a lowly follower or underling who does another's bidding.

clue.text: Spot-on article about a minister

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a curate is a clergyman, a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a clergyman that gets the facts exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spot-on is exactly correct, without error.

clue.text: A rider that is accepting toll has some attraction

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside, so the bell sound goes within the added note

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, like PS, a postscript
to toll a bell is to sound a peal

explanation.surface: A horseman who pays a road toll turns out to be rather alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' and 'toll' suggest a horseman on a turnpike; a rider is also a clause added to a document, here PS.
explanation.definitionFit: If something appeals to you it holds an attraction or interest for you.

clue.text: Raised by a sovereign?

parts.note: reads like money collected in gold coins, but describes a commoner lifted to the peerage by the monarch

explanation.surface: A sum of money collected in gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin, and a noble was another coin, which adds to the misdirection toward money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made a peer by the Crown has been raised in rank, given a title by the monarch.

clue.text: Urge to put studies be fore exercise

indicators.note: the clue's split 'before' places the studying piece ahead of the exercise piece

parts.note: to con a text is to study it, so cons means studies
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Advice to put homework ahead of sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to press or compel them to act, a strong sense of urge.

clue.text: Up it goes for viewers in the main

definitions.text: Up it goes for viewers in the main

parts.words: Up it goes for viewers in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea; a submarine raises this sighting tube so those below can look out above the waves

explanation.surface: Something hoisted so that the bulk of an audience can see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, not 'the majority'.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's viewing tube is raised above the surface so the crew below can see.

clue.text: Being trendy, acquired a pig

parts.note: something trendy is in fashion, or in
acquired means got

explanation.surface: A fashionable farmer buys a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' looks like the animal, but a pig is also a block of cast metal, as in pig iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is an oblong mass of cast metal, the same thing as a bar of smelted metal.

clue.text: A hideaway in the Near East

definitions.note: the definition stands for a place located in that region

parts.note: a den is a hidden lair or retreat

explanation.surface: A secret retreat somewhere in the Levant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Working out latitude and height

indicators.note: working out suggests calculation, but here the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A navigator calculates position and elevation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' reads as calculating, which suits latitude, but it signals that LATITUDE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Altitude is the elevation of something above sea level.

clue.text: Involved in one-sided rows, eventually nod

indicators.note: the letters needed are tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: After lopsided arguments, someone finally dozes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the end of 'sided', all of 'rows' and the start of 'eventually'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to doze, to be half asleep.

clue.text: Old Peruvian taking a single can maybe

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the word can might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An ancient Andean picks up one tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you to rearrange CAN into NCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire in the Andes, centred on Peru, before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: A letter with cutting amusing comeback

indicators.note: one piece cutting into another sits inside it
a comeback turns the word for amusing round to read backwards

parts.note: droll means amusing in a dry way
and means together with

explanation.surface: A note containing a witty, biting retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A letter' is one who lets property, not a written message. 'Comeback' turns the amusing word into LLORD, and 'cutting' means the joining word splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A property owner lets rooms or houses to tenants, so is literally one who lets.

clue.text: Unpolluted space for players' use

definitions.note: the definition is a place set aside for actors' use

parts.note: green describes what is environmentally clean, unpolluted
room means space

explanation.surface: Clean, fresh air reserved for sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sport, but they are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's waiting lounge is where actors relax before and between their scenes.

clue.text: After the game hundreds made complaint

indicators.note: the hundreds piece comes after the bird in the answer

parts.note: grouse is a game bird
D is the Roman numeral 500, five hundreds

explanation.surface: Once the match was over, crowds lodged a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The game' suggests a match, but it is game in the hunting sense, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble or moan.

clue.text: Mounting a revolt

definitions.meaning: mounting here means rising up, ascending
a rebellion by people against their rulers

explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is literally a rising up, and a popular rebellion is a rising of the people.

clue.text: Part-exchange can include novel read

indicators.note: the word for can includes the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word read appears in a new order

explanation.surface: A secondhand dealer's tin box holds a new book to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal, making RADE, and 'include' means the container holds those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as part payment for a new one.

clue.text: Watched a dredger in operation

indicators.note: in operation suggests machinery working, signalling the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stood observing a dredging boat at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In operation' rearranges A and DREDGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it attentively.

clue.text: Check a crawler without cash

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the creature goes round the money

parts.note: an insect is a creeping creature, a crawler
P, for penny or pence, stands for a little cash

explanation.surface: Examine a penniless bootlicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside'. 'Crawler' suggests a toady, but it is a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to check over.

clue.text: Puts up with relatives-should be on guard

parts.note: bears means tolerates or puts up with
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone who tolerates family must stay alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On guard' means watchful, but the tall fur cap is worn on the heads of British Guards soldiers on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall black fur hat is worn by Guards regiments on ceremonial sentry duty.

clue.text: Understanding the German issue

definitions.meaning: the German word for a child, one's issue or offspring

explanation.definitionFit: Kind means considerate and sympathetic, and in German Kind means child, the same as offspring.

clue.text: Fight for breath, as admitted by the doctor

indicators.note: the little word is let in, taken inside the doctor's letters

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to breathe when the doctor lets them in.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to struggle for air, drawing breath sharply.

clue.text: May set out to appear sultry

indicators.note: out signals that the two words are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: May begins and promises hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is a month in the surface, but its letters join SET for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy weather is hot and humid, as is sultry weather.

clue.text: If reflective and close he's a real trial

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the little word is turned backwards

parts.note: a close is an end

explanation.surface: A thoughtful moment and a quiet finish to a difficult man's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil or monster is someone who torments others.

clue.text: Porridge is a fine alternative!

parts.note: porridge is British slang for time served; a jail term is a sentence imposed instead of a fine

explanation.surface: Oatmeal recommended as a good breakfast swap.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a jail term, and a judge may choose that rather than a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge means serving time, and jail is the punishment often imposed in place of a money penalty.

clue.text: Railway worker in a Manx resort

parts.note: a porter carries luggage at a station

explanation.surface: A station porter employed at an Isle of Man holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Erin is a seaside resort on the Isle of Man; Manx means of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Erin is a seaside holiday town on the island's south-west coast.

clue.text: Start to cast

clue.text: To inform about top people is squealing

indicators.note: the word for informing goes about, around, the elite

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
the cream are the best, the elite

explanation.surface: Grassing on the elite is ratting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squealing' joins the informing image, but it is the definition, a high cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieking at high pitch is squealing loudly.
